scenes.title: What Is the Internet?
scenes.explanation: The internet is a worldwide network of interconnected computer networks.
scenes.takeaway: The internet connects networks, not just devices.

scenes.title: Devices and Connections
scenes.explanation: Phones, laptops, and servers exchange information through wired and wireless connections.
scenes.takeaway: Every device needs a path to communicate.

scenes.title: Data Becomes Packets
scenes.explanation: Large messages are divided into small pieces called packets before transmission.
scenes.takeaway: Packets make communication manageable.

scenes.title: IP Addresses
scenes.explanation: Network devices use Internet Protocol addresses to route data to destinations.
scenes.takeaway: IP addresses help data find its destination.

scenes.title: Domain Names
scenes.explanation: Human-friendly names are translated into network addresses using DNS.
scenes.takeaway: DNS links names to addresses.

scenes.title: Routers and Paths
scenes.explanation: Routers forward packets between networks, selecting suitable next hops.
scenes.takeaway: Routers connect separate networks.

scenes.title: The Role of Servers
scenes.explanation: Servers respond to requests and provide web pages, media, and other services.
scenes.takeaway: Servers provide resources on demand.

scenes.title: Clients Make Requests
scenes.explanation: A browser or app sends a request and receives a response from a service.
scenes.takeaway: Clients request; servers respond.

scenes.title: HTTP and HTTPS
scenes.explanation: Web applications commonly communicate using HTTP; HTTPS adds encrypted transport.
scenes.takeaway: HTTPS protects data in transit.

scenes.title: Encryption Basics
scenes.explanation: Encryption transforms readable information into data that requires a key to interpret.
scenes.takeaway: Encryption helps protect privacy.

scenes.title: Wi-Fi and Mobile Networks
scenes.explanation: Local wireless links connect devices to networks that reach the broader internet.
scenes.takeaway: Wireless access is only one part of the route.

scenes.title: Fiber-Optic Connections
scenes.explanation: Fiber cables carry information as light over long distances.
scenes.takeaway: Light can transport data at high capacity.

scenes.title: Undersea Cables
scenes.explanation: Submarine cables carry much of the world's international internet traffic.
scenes.takeaway: Global connectivity relies on physical infrastructure.

scenes.title: Latency and Bandwidth
scenes.explanation: Latency measures delay, while bandwidth describes potential transfer capacity.
scenes.takeaway: Speed has more than one dimension.

scenes.title: Caching Content
scenes.explanation: Caches store frequently requested content closer to users to reduce repeated work.
scenes.takeaway: Caching can reduce delays.

scenes.title: Content Delivery Networks
scenes.explanation: Distributed servers deliver content from locations closer to viewers.
scenes.takeaway: CDNs improve delivery efficiency.

scenes.title: How Streaming Works
scenes.explanation: Video players request compressed media in small segments as playback continues.
scenes.takeaway: Streaming transfers media progressively.

scenes.title: Why Connections Fail
scenes.explanation: Outages may involve local equipment, routing, servers, or service providers.
scenes.takeaway: Troubleshooting starts by locating the fault.

scenes.title: Online Safety
scenes.explanation: Updates, strong authentication, and careful link handling reduce common risks.
scenes.takeaway: Safe habits matter at every layer.

scenes.title: Putting It All Together
scenes.explanation: Your device, local network, routers, servers, and protocols cooperate on each request.
scenes.takeaway: The internet works through many connected systems.
